title: Watch Specification v1
description: Cadence policy for one InfoItem: how often the cluster wants it checked. Archiver owns this document (declared intent); Watcher owns execution (when the fetch actually fires) and keeps a local fallback cadence for a spec it cannot parse. CADENCE ONLY: active/paused is NOT in here — it is the sibling column info_items.watch_active, projected to the announcement's envelope-level 'active' beside 'revoked'. That separation is load-bearing twice over: a policy document shared across items could not carry per-item pause state, and nested inside an untyped dict the three-state distinction (revoked / paused / scheduled) had no contract-level schema guarantee. BOUNDARY: a WatchSpec is per-item cadence. content.fetch-policy is per-host spacing — different key, stream, owner, and consumer. Both answer 'how often do we hit things' and will attract merge proposals; they are not the same knob and must not be merged. The document is singular, not a list: source_specs is plural because Watcher walks it as a fallback loop, and a WatchSpec has no fallback semantics — one policy is in effect. It is carried resolved on the wire, never as a reference, so a future reusable-policy table stays an Archiver-internal change.

interval.description: Watcher interval string. Optional: when absent, the consumer applies its own default, which may be a per-domain default_schedule_config rather than a global constant. The pattern is the grammar Watcher's parse_interval accepts; the narrower set the dashboard offers (1h/6h/1d/7d) lives in src/dashboard/cadence.py.
